name: Chime Bells from the Tomb of Marques Yi of Zeng State
description: Chimes, ancient percussion instruments made of bronze, emerged in the Western Zhou Dynasty and flourished from the Spring and Autumn Period and the Warring States Period until the Qin and Han Dynasties. Among the currently unearthed cultural relics, Zeng Hou Yi’s Chime Bells are the largest, best-preserved, most complete-rhythm, and most magnificent set of chimes discovered in China so far. They represent the advanced level of ancient Chinese music. It is a national first-level protected cultural relic. With the broadcast of the "National Treasure" column, it has once again entered people's field of vision. Pinku joins hands with Wuxitang to reproduce classics and historical treasures, taking you to listen to the romantic echoes that have traveled through thousands of years.
